name: Valle de Cuelgamuros (former Valle de los Caídos)
story: Franco ordered this basilica cut into the granite of the Guadarrama, crowned by a 150 m cross, as a monument to his victory. Work lasted from 1940 to 1959; the workforce included political prisoners who redeemed sentence by labour. Remains of tens of thousands of dead from both sides were brought here, many Republicans moved from mass graves without their families' consent. Franco himself was buried here in 1975 and exhumed in 2019; José Antonio Primo de Rivera was removed in 2023. The Democratic Memory Law (Ley 20/2022) changed the official name from Valle de los Caídos to Valle de Cuelgamuros, made it a Place of Democratic Memory and plans its re-signification; forensic exhumations in the crypts continue.
see: The monumental esplanade, the rock-cut basilica and the 150 m cross (the funicular up to the cross is closed indefinitely), with the Benedictine abbey behind.
plan: Paid entry; closed Mondays and some holidays. Opening days and prices change, so check the Patrimonio Nacional website just before you go. Access by car via the M-600 from El Escorial; allow half a day with El Escorial. Dress respectfully: it is an active church.

boxes.text: Numbers vary: around 33,800 people are recorded as interred; how many prisoners worked on the building is disputed (official records of a few hundred convicts at a time, against estimates of up to 20,000 over the whole project).
